response: Yes, telmisartan has been shown to prevent hepatic fibrosis in rats with alloxan-induced diabetes. Telmisartan, an angiotensin II receptor antagonist, has been found to have anti-fibrotic effects in various studies, including those involving diabetic models. Its mechanism of action involves reducing oxidative stress, inflammation, and fibrogenesis, which are key factors in the development of hepatic fibrosis. By blocking the angiotensin II receptor, telmisartan can mitigate the progression of liver fibrosis in diabetic rats, suggesting its potential therapeutic benefits in preventing or treating hepatic fibrosis associated with diabetes.
